category_title: Students who demonstrate high engagement and responsiveness to visual schedules
minimal_context: The student is standing on a spot in the gym practicing catching a ball with two hands.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start our next activity. Please stand on your spot.

STUDENT: (Gets the picture schedule out again to see what's next) Catch.

TUTOR: Yes. Hands out, look at the ball. (Tosses the ball)

STUDENT: (Catches with two hands, squeezes the ball, then smiles and jumps up and down because she is really excited)

TUTOR: Okay, let's do another one. Look over here and listen to me.

STUDENT: (Looks away at the visual stimuli in the room, seeing things and not focusing on what the teacher is trying to say)

options.A: Adjust expectations for how much instruction the student can handle during the session and avoid introducing new activities.
options.B: Have the student complete reflective journal entries in which they are encouraged to write or draw freely about their APE experience.
options.C: Show the student how to use the ball appropriately (e.g., keep it in their hands, set it on the spot when not in use, and squeeze it when anxious).
options.D: Establish communication protocols within the school environment and focus on building a strong staff-student relationship over time.
